title: Kingdom of Scotland
capsule: The Kingdom of Scotland emerged as a coherent monarchy in the 9th–10th centuries from the Kingdom of Alba and was recognised internationally by the late 11th century under Malcolm III and his successors. The Wars of Scottish Independence (1296–1328) against English claims were decisive: Robert I (the Bruce) secured de facto independence at Bannockburn (1314) and legal recognition by the Treaty of Edinburgh-Northampton (1328). The crown passed to the Stuart dynasty, and in 1603 James VI inherited the English throne (Union of the Crowns); the parliamentary union with England creating Great Britain followed in 1707.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Scotland's borders with England were broadly stable after the 12th century and are well documented in treaty and chronicle sources, though exact frontier demarcations in the Western Isles and northern highlands evolved through the 13th–15th centuries.
